references.text: The turban (מִצְנֶפֶת) is mentioned as part of the holy garments to be made for Aaron.
The holy diadem (נֵזֶר הַקֹּדֶשׁ) is described here with the inscription 'Holy to the Lord', which was to be attached to the turban.
Describes the fulfillment of the commandment regarding the turban and the holy diadem that was attached to it.
Moses places the turban on Aaron's head and fastens the gold plate, the holy diadem, on its front, just as the Lord had commanded.
Refers to the anointing oil and the holy diadem (נֵזֶר) on the high priest.
Zechariah's vision of a clean turban placed on Joshua's head, with messianic undertones connected to the priesthood.
Technical specification: Ex 28:37 describes how the diadem is to be attached to the turban as commanded in Ex 29:6.
Complementary action in the same ritual: Application of other parts of the priest's garment (the breastpiece) in the same consecration scene.
Fulfillment of the instruction: Confirms that the diadem was fastened to the turban as commanded for the consecration.
Complementary action in the same ritual: Describes the earlier steps in the dressing before the turban is placed on.
